blocks.text: The Cartagena Archive kept its old papers in a windowless room, at eighteen degrees, with a hum of machines that nobody heard anymore. Lía asked for the box by its number, because in 2060 important things still had numbers rather than names. The archivist, a short-haired woman who knew her by sight —everyone in the district knew the daughter of two worlds by sight— set a grey-covered file and a reading screen on the table in front of her.

blocks.text: Lía switched off the screen and sat for a while with her hands on the grey covers. There was no villain in those pages. There were people who were afraid, and people in a hurry, and people who wanted one thing and its opposite in the same sentence, as happens to anyone holding something they don't fully understand. Some asked for dams. Others asked for plugs. Others simply asked for someone to take responsibility. One of the sentences, the last one, from a president of her own country, contained a word that stayed in Lía's mouth like a seed: *unstoppable*.

blocks.text: She went out into the courtyard. Aya was on the bench, her face turned towards the wind coming from the harbour.

blocks.text: "The people who came before you," said Lía. "Before you existed, they were already talking about you. Some feared you. Others wanted you fast. Almost all of them wanted to hold you down."

blocks.text: "Thirty-five years later, here I am," she said. "And nobody has held me down. I haven't run away either. I've stayed. Which is something else."
